text: {"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strncasecmp() in lib/string.c advanced `s1` backwards (`*s1--`) instead of forwards, so it read the wrong bytes; changed it to `*s1++` to match `s2`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string.c"], "summary": "strcspn() in lib/string.c advanced its loop with `--p` instead of `++p`, so it scanned backwards past the start of the string; changed it to `++p`, which makes the string_test_strspn reject-length assertions pass."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_get_size(), the loop that reduces a large `size` by the divisor decremented the unit index `i` instead of incrementing it, so huge sizes such as 2^64-1 produced a wrong unit (e.g. \"UNK\" instead of \"ZB\"); changed `i--` to `i++` at lib/string_helpers.c:88."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_escape_mem() the input loop read bytes with `*src--`, walking backwards from the start of the buffer; changed it to `*src++` so each input byte is read forward once, which fixes the escape KUnit mismatch."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/string_helpers.c"], "summary": "In string_unescape() the escape-detection check was inverted (`src[1] == '\\0'` instead of `src[1] != '\\0'`), so backslash escapes were never decoded and were copied through literally, producing one extra output byte per escape sequence; changed it to `src[1] != '\\0'`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "get_option() decremented `cur` (`--cur`) instead of incrementing it (`++cur`) when parsing a leading hyphen, so a negative number after a comma such as \"-3\" in \"0-1,-3,6\" was read from the comma and rejected, truncating the parsed list to two values; the fix is changing `--cur` to `++cur`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In get_options() the loop exit condition was inverted (`if (res != 1) break;`), so it stopped at every comma (res 2) and range hyphen (res 3); changing it to `if (res == 1) break;` makes parsing continue after commas and ranges, as the range-handling comment and the test expectations require."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/cmdline.c"], "summary": "In memparse(), the 'G' suffix case used `ret << 10;` (a discarded shift, which is the -Wunused-value warning) instead of `ret <<= 10;`, so gigabyte sizes such as `mem=1G` were not scaled correctly; changed it to the compound assignment."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In `__siphash_aligned`, the tail-length mask was `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)` (mask 6), which dropped the trailing byte whenever len % 8 is odd; changed it to `sizeof(u64) - 1` (mask 7) to match `__siphash_unaligned`."}

{"changed_files": ["lib/siphash.c"], "summary": "In the 64-bit `__hsiphash_aligned` (lib/siphash.c ~line 250), the tail length mask was `len & (sizeof(u64) - 2)`, which is `len & 6` and drops bit 0; it is now `len & (sizeof(u64) - 1)` (`len & 7`), so lengths with a 1, 3, 5 or 7-byte tail (e.g. 57, 59, 61, 63) hash their final bytes correctly."}
